chamber.title: The Chamber
chamber.lead: A professional body belonging to UTICA and the National Health Federation, the Chamber brings Tunisia's private clinics together around a shared ambition: quality care that is accessible and trustworthy.
chamber.mission_lead: Represent the profession, defend its interests and contribute, alongside public authorities, to the quality of the Tunisian health system.
chamber.m1: Speak for private clinics before the Ministry of Health, CNAM and other institutions.
chamber.m2: Negotiate agreements and help shape the sector's regulatory framework.
chamber.m3: Inform and advise members on regulation, quality, human resources and investment.
chamber.m4: Showcase Tunisian healthcare in Tunisia and abroad.
chamber.board_lead: The executive board is elected by the general assembly of members. Composition to be completed.
chamber.statutes_html: The Chamber is governed by its statutes and internal rules, within the framework of the statutes of UTICA and the National Health Federation. Any licensed private healthcare facility operating in Tunisia may join.
chamber.history_html:
1. Date to be completedCreation of the Chamber within UTICA.
  2. Date to be completedKey milestones: agreements, reforms, events.
  3. 2026Adoption of a visual identity and launch of the official website and social media.
chamber.governance_lead: The Chamber is run by bodies elected by its members, within the framework of the statutes of UTICA and the National Health Federation.
chamber.ag: Brings together all member clinics. It elects the executive board, sets the main orientations and may be convened in extraordinary session.
chamber.bureau: Elected by the general assembly, it leads the Chamber's work and represents it before public authorities and partners.
chamber.team_lead: The permanent team follows up on files, supports members and handles the Chamber's communications. Composition to be completed.

patient.title: Patients
patient.lead: Clear guidance to stay well informed before, during and after your stay in a clinic.
patient.rights_html:
In every private clinic, you are entitled to:

  • Information: clear explanations about your health, the proposed care, its risks and alternatives.
  • Consent: no procedure may be performed without your free and informed consent, except in life-threatening emergencies.
  • Free choice of your doctor and your facility.
  • Confidentiality: medical secrecy protects all information about you.
  • Access to your medical record and to the reports of your tests and procedures.
  • Prior information on costs: ask for a detailed quote before any planned hospital stay.
  • Dignity and respect for your privacy, beliefs and pain.
patient.bill_html:
A clinic bill usually has two separate parts: clinic fees and medical fees.

ItemWhat it covers
StayRoom, accommodation, meals, nursing care, per day.
Operating theatreTheatre, equipment, theatre staff.
Pharmacy and suppliesMedicines, medical devices, any prostheses and implants.
TestsLaboratory tests, imaging, investigations.
Medical feesSurgeon, anaesthetist, other doctors — often billed separately.
Good practice: compare the final bill with the quote. Any difference should be explained to you (complication, longer stay, additional test).
patient.cover_html:
CNAM

Depending on the scheme chosen with CNAM (the National Health Insurance Fund) and the agreements in force, some procedures and hospital stays in private clinics may be covered in full or in part. Coverage usually requires prior approval from CNAM.

  1. Check your entitlementUp-to-date membership and chosen scheme (public, private or reimbursement).
  2. Request prior approvalWith your medical file and the clinic's quote, before admission.
  3. Present the approval on admissionThe clinic then applies direct billing for the covered share.

Supplementary insurance

Your group insurance or mutual fund may top up CNAM reimbursement. Check ceilings, deadlines and required documents, and whether the clinic has a direct-billing agreement with your insurer.
patient.claim_html:
Most issues are resolved directly with the facility. Recommended steps:

  1. Contact the clinicWrite to the management or the quality / patient relations department, describing the facts and enclosing supporting documents.
  2. Wait for a written replyThe facility must review your request and respond.
  3. Contact the ChamberIf the dispute with a member clinic persists, the Chamber can offer mediation.
  4. Other remediesDepending on the issue: Ministry of Health, National Council of the Medical Association, CNAM or your insurer.
patient.disclaimer: General information for guidance only, to be validated by the Chamber. It does not replace the regulations in force or advice from your fund or insurer.

travel.title: Get treatment in Tunisia
travel.lead: Modern clinics, recognised doctors and a warm welcome, a few hours' flight from Europe, North Africa and sub-Saharan Africa.
travel.w1: Specialists often trained in Tunisia and abroad, and teams experienced in caring for international patients.
travel.w2: Two to three hours' flight from most European capitals, with regular connections to Africa and the Middle East.
travel.w3: Competitive prices, announced in advance through a detailed quote, for care that meets international standards.
travel.w4: Up-to-date facilities: imaging, operating theatres, interventional cardiology, haemodialysis.
travel.w5: Care in Arabic, French and English, and often Italian or German.
travel.w6: Mild climate, a tradition of thalassotherapy and a wide range of hotels for a peaceful recovery.
travel.spec_html:
• Cosmetic and reconstructive surgery
  • Orthopaedics and spine surgery
  • Ophthalmology and refractive surgery
  • Cardiology and cardiovascular surgery
  • Assisted reproduction
  • Haemodialysis during your stay
  • Comprehensive health check-ups
travel.steps_html:
• First contactSend your medical file to the clinic chosen from the directory.
  • Medical opinion and quoteThe doctor reviews your file; the clinic sends you a detailed quote.
  • Travel and stayWelcome, hospital stay and follow-up by the medical team.
  • Return and follow-upA medical report is handed over at discharge for your own doctor.
travel.advice_html:
Our advice before you travel

  • Contact a member clinic directly and ask for a detailed written quote.
  • Check whether your insurer or health fund may cover the treatment.
  • Ask for the name and specialty of the doctor who will treat you.
  • Plan a long enough stay for post-operative follow-up before flying home.
